In [[Riemannian geometry]], the '''smooth coarea formulas''' relate integrals over the domain of certain mappings with integrals over their codomains.

Let <math>\scriptstyle M,\,N</math> be smooth [[Riemannian manifold]]s of respective dimensions <math>\scriptstyle m\,\geq\, n</math>. Let <math>\scriptstyle F:M\,\longrightarrow\, N</math> be a smooth [[surjection]] such that the [[pushforward (differential)]] of <math>\scriptstyle F</math> is surjective almost everywhere. Let <math>\scriptstyle\varphi:M\,\longrightarrow\, [0,\infty)</math> a [[measurable function]]. Then, the following two equalities hold:

:<math>\int_{x\in M}\varphi(x)\,dM = \int_{y\in N}\int_{x\in F^{-1}(y)}\varphi(x)\frac{1}{N\!J\;F(x)}\,dF^{-1}(y)\,dN</math>

:<math>\int_{x\in M}\varphi(x)N\!J\;F(x)\,dM = \int_{y\in N}\int_{x\in F^{-1}(y)} \varphi(x)\,dF^{-1}(y)\,dN</math>

where  <math>\scriptstyle N\!J\;F(x)</math> is the [[Jacobian matrix and determinant|normal Jacobian]] of <math>\scriptstyle F</math>, i.e. the determinant of the derivative restricted to the orthogonal complement of its kernel.

Note that from [[Sard's lemma]] almost every point <math>\scriptstyle y\,\in\, N</math> is a regular point of <math>\scriptstyle F</math> and hence the set <math>\scriptstyle F^{-1}(y)</math> is a Riemannian submanifold of <math>\scriptstyle M</math>, so the integrals in the right-hand side of the formulas above make sense.

==References==
*Chavel, Isaac (2006) ''Riemannian Geometry. A Modern Introduction. Second Edition''.
